text: Every mould in this factory makes heat. This is where it goes.
Hot water from the process is pumped to the top,
and sprayed over the fill: thin sheets that spread it into a film.
A fan pulls air up through the fill.
A little water evaporates, and that carries the heat away.
Cooled water collects in the basin, and goes back to the moulds.
But evaporation only removes pure water. The minerals stay behind.
The open tower also scrubs dust from the air, and sunlight grows algae.
Every pass, the water gets harder and dirtier.
Minerals come out as scale on the hottest surfaces: your mould cooling channels.
Scale insulates. Moulds run hotter, and cycle time creeps up.
Warning signs: rising conductivity in the tower water, and drifting cycle times.
So: bleed off a little water, and top up with fresh.
Treat it to stop scale, corrosion and algae.
Filter it, and clean the basin, fill and nozzles on schedule.
